hook.line: Doña Eulalia wants the family to make peace now, and Joaquín wanted exactly the same thing before he died. Spanish shows the time on the second verb as well as the first, so hear the two side by side.
hook.es: Joaquín quería que la familia hiciera las paces.
hook.en: Joaquín wanted the family to make peace.

examples.es: Vale quiere que Tomás se quede.
Vale quería que Tomás se quedara.
Me sorprende que Mariana no llamara.
Me dijo que lo llame esta tarde.
examples.en: He told me to call him this afternoon.

rule:
Look at the clock. What decides the second verb is when that second thing happens.

Say the second half on its own, then find its subjunctive.

*Viene* or *vendrá*: now, or still ahead. That gives the present subjunctive, *venga*.
*Quiero que vengas.* *Me alegra que estés aquí.*

*Vino*, *venía* or *vendría*: already over, or still ahead of a moment back then. That gives the *-ra* form, *viniera*.
*Me alegra que vinieras ayer.* *Quería que vinieras.* *Me pidió que me quedara.*

So a present opening can take *-ra*, when the thing is over. *Me sorprende que Mariana no llamara.*

A past opening can take the present, when the thing is still ahead today. *Me dijo que lo llame esta tarde.* This afternoon hasn't come yet.

One limit: *quiero que* and *pido que* look ahead, so they don't go with *-ra*.

English hides most of this: "I want you to come" and "I wanted you to come" both keep "come".
smallPrint: Teachers call this the sequence of tenses. It isn't a matching rule between the two verbs. It's the same past, present or future you'd use without the opening, moved into the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say "I want you to come." Choose *vengas* or *vinieras*, then type it: *Quiero que ___.*
yourTurn.why: You want it now and the coming is still ahead, so the present subjunctive: *vengas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say "I wanted you to come." Choose *vengas* or *vinieras*, then type it: *Quería que ___.*
yourTurn.why: The wanting is over, and the coming was still ahead of it back then, so the *-ra* form: *vinieras*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "Vale wants Tomás to stay."
yourTurn.answer: Vale quiere que Tomás se quede.
yourTurn.why: The staying is still ahead, so *se quede*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it past: *Vale quiere que Tomás se quede.* Say "Vale wanted Tomás to stay."
yourTurn.answer: Vale quería que Tomás se quedara.
yourTurn.why: Back then the staying was still ahead, so *se quedara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it present: *Me pidió que me quedara.* Say "He asks me to stay."
yourTurn.why: The staying is still ahead today, so *quede*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: "Do you want me to help you?"
yourTurn.why: It's still ahead of this moment, so *ayude*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: "Did you want me to help you?"
yourTurn.why: The offer was back then, so the helping was still ahead of that moment: *ayudara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it past: *Prefiero que cierres la puerta.* Say "I preferred you to close the door."
accept: Prefería que tú cerraras la puerta.
yourTurn.why: *Prefiero* becomes *prefería*. The closing was still ahead of that moment, so *cerraras*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "I'm glad you came yesterday."
accept: Me alegra que hayas venido ayer.
Me alegro de que vinieras ayer.
Me alegro de que hayas venido ayer.
yourTurn.why: *Me alegra* is now, but the coming is over, so *vinieras*. *Hayas venido* works too.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "I'm surprised Mariana didn't call."
yourTurn.answer: Me sorprende que Mariana no llamara.
accept: Me sorprende que Mariana no haya llamado.
yourTurn.why: The surprise is now, but the call is over: without the opening it's *no llamó*, so *no llamara*. *No haya llamado* works too.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The feeling is now, but *ayer* is over: *viniste* gives *vinieras*. Don't copy the time of the first verb.
You can't want now what's already over, so after *quiero* the coming is still ahead: *vengas*.
Wanting looks ahead, so the helping is still to come: *ayude*.
*Vienes* says it's so. *Quería que* holds the idea up, and from back then it was still ahead: *vinieras*.

personal: Type two sentences about one person: one about what they want now (*Mi mamá quiere que...*) and one about what they wanted when you were younger (*Mi mamá quería que...*).
